standard.title: Control of Air Pollution in Coal-Based Thermal Power Plant — Code of Practice
standard.sector: Environment and Ecology / Air, Soil and Noise Pollution Control

sectional_committee.name: Air, Soil and Noise Pollution Control Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the code of practice containing guidelines, engineering strategies, and technical criteria for controlling and abating air pollution emissions originating from coal-based thermal power plants, particularly pulverized fuel fired power stations, to systematically reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) footprints and local atmospheric pollutants.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the code of practice containing guidelines, engineering strategies, and technical criteria for controlling and abating air pollution emissions originating from coal-based thermal power plants, particularly pulverized fuel fired power stations, to systematically reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) footprints and local atmospheric pollutants.

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 19767:2026 is an engineering guideline and operational code of practice for thermal power plants rather than a direct consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product certification stamp. However, compliance with its technical specifications, stack heights, and emissions control strategies is legally enforced across India by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs) under Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) statutory notifications to authorize a utility's Consent to Operate (CTO). Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.
requirements: Establishes structured guidelines and technical criteria to design, implement, and optimize air pollution control systems specifically to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) and fine particulate emissions from pulverized fuel fired power stations.
Outlines engineering considerations for installing in-line carbon dioxide (CO2) capture units to physically trap carbon emissions from boiler flue gases before they are released into the atmosphere.

Captured carbon dioxide can be directly used as a source for conversion to industrial chemicals, additives, and other value-added products, enabling carbon recycling and supporting national circular economy initiatives.

Provides technical guidelines for the design, selection, and maintenance of high-capacity Electrostatic Precipitators (ESPs) and fabric filter baghouses to trap flying coal ash and keep particulate matter (PM) emissions below statutory boundaries.

Specifies process and engineering requirements for wet, semi-dry, or dry flue gas desulfurization systems utilizing alkaline sorbents (like limestone) to scrub and neutralize sulfur dioxide (SO2) from combustion flues.

Regulates the implementation of low-NOx burners, overfire air (OFA) systems, or secondary post-combustion treatments (such as Selective Catalytic Reduction, SCR, or Selective Non-Catalytic Reduction, SNCR) to control thermal and fuel NOx generation.
Mandates high-elevation chimneys and stack designs to facilitate maximum atmospheric dispersion of residual flue gases, preventing ground-level accumulation of pollutants near local habitats.
